title: From site to service
contentStatus: Public capability evidence with illustrative project-value mechanisms
scopeStatus: Illustrative campus · Project scope to confirm
lifecycleNote: These twelve stages are overlapping workstreams, not a universal serial programme. The seven chapters are a client narrative rather than a Bird-published workflow.
focusNote: Grey means not the current focus. It does not mean a scope is outside Bird. Use the role label to distinguish responsibilities.
valueMechanismNote: Each value mechanism is an illustrative application to this campus, conditional on agreed scope and project conditions. It is not a measured result, project commitment or guarantee.
evidenceNote: Sources are public Bird pages and Bird-hosted documents reviewed in the supplied evidence register. Evidence for capability and illustrative client-value mechanisms remain distinct.
testingNote: B9 supports industrial high-voltage testing and commissioning as self-perform capability. B1 supports data-centre commissioning support. Neither establishes full data-centre IST, independent certification or owner-acceptance responsibility.

lenses.label: Schedule
lenses.qualification: No project duration or acceleration is calculated or guaranteed

lenses.label: Cost certainty
lenses.qualification: No saving, fixed price or cost certainty level is promised

lenses.label: Risk
lenses.qualification: Technical interfaces and external dependencies remain

lenses.label: Safety
lenses.qualification: Planning mechanism only; no incident-reduction claim

lenses.label: Coordination
lenses.qualification: Actual responsibilities depend on the agreed project scope

chapters.label: Overview
chapters.headline: From groundworks to critical systems
chapters.description: One integrated self-perform team, from power to white space
chapters.context: The opening previews power infrastructure. Continue to planning to follow the overlapping delivery stages.

chapters.label: Planning
chapters.headline: Buildability. Before breaking ground.
chapters.description: Direct trade expertise, earlier in the plan
chapters.context: Design, procurement, energy and approvals can progress together. Utility decisions and permit authority remain external.

chapters.label: Civil
chapters.headline: Groundwork. Direct control.
chapters.description: Connect below-ground work with the systems it receives
chapters.context: Selecting a scope reveals its workface and retained inspection points. Actual delivery boundaries need agreement.

chapters.label: Systems
chapters.headline: Critical systems. Connected delivery.
chapters.description: Explore the trades inside the same facility
chapters.context: Only the selected scope is in colour. White-space deployment is a delivery offering; its full trade allocation is not established.

chapters.label: Connections
chapters.headline: The advantage is in the connections
chapters.description: Connect the trades that depend on each other
chapters.context: Potential value depends on agreed scope and project conditions. Internal interfaces, inspections and external approvals remain.

chapters.label: Readiness
chapters.headline: Ready is proven.
chapters.description: Keep testing, commissioning support and acceptance distinct
chapters.context: Industrial HV testing is a documented self-perform capability. Full data-centre IST, independent commissioning authority and owner acceptance are separate responsibilities to establish.

chapters.label: Next phase
chapters.headline: Built for what comes next.
chapters.description: Connect today's delivery to tomorrow's growth
chapters.sceneState: Operating facility and next-phase work area
chapters.context: Expansion and general industrial maintenance are documented capabilities. Data-centre operation, IT ownership and service-level obligations are not established.

stages.label: Define and establish feasibility
stages.description: Owner requirements, site constraints, specialist studies and delivery intent
stages.boundary: Bird can contribute preconstruction expertise; feasibility conclusions and owner requirements remain project-specific

stages.label: Plan and permit
stages.description: Entitlement, environmental and construction approvals; stakeholder and utility gates
stages.boundary: Bird/Stack describes managing permitting in an adjacent modular offer; no data-centre permit authority or approval control is established

stages.label: Power and energy strategy
stages.description: Generation, HV/MV routes, substations, grid and thermal interfaces
stages.boundary: Infrastructure delivery does not establish energy availability, grid connection rights, utility approval or power pricing

stages.label: Design, procure and fabricate
stages.description: Buildability, BIM/VDC, long-lead releases, logistics and fabrication
stages.boundary: Design responsibility, equipment selection, capacity and procurement commitments require project agreement

stages.label: Enabling works and civil
stages.description: Access, earthworks, site services and construction workfaces
stages.boundary: Project conditions, permitted work areas and actual direct-delivery split remain to confirm

stages.label: Build below grade and foundations
stages.description: Buried services, duct routes, excavation and concrete interfaces
stages.boundary: Concrete formwork evidence does not establish every foundation, geotechnical or structural package

stages.label: Structure and enclosure
stages.description: Structural delivery, weather-tightness and equipment access
stages.boundary: Civil/structural delivery is documented; whole steel and envelope self-performance is not established

stages.label: Install plant and M&E
stages.description: Electrical, mechanical, HVAC/refrigeration and thermal interfaces
stages.boundary: Equipment supply, manufacturer warranties and the detailed installation split remain separate

stages.label: Fit out white space and controls
stages.description: White space, telecom and operator controls, fire, security and IT interfaces
stages.boundary: Telecom self-performance does not establish every controls, security, fire, rack or IT package

stages.label: Test, commission and prove
stages.description: Package tests, commissioning support, integrated-test context and acceptance gates
stages.boundary: Separate industrial HV testing from full data-centre IST, independent certification, utility energization and owner acceptance

stages.label: Turn over, operate and maintain
stages.description: Handover, owner/operator readiness, maintenance and access
stages.boundary: No project-specific operating SLA, training package, facilities operation, IT service or uptime obligation is established

stages.label: Expand, retrofit and renew
stages.description: Live-site expansion, retained access, renewal and future end-of-life planning
stages.boundary: Specific renewal, decommissioning, circularity and disposal services require separate scope confirmation

scopes.label: Generation
scopes.headline: Connect generation construction with the campus plan
scopes.documentedCapability: Bird lists power generation within integrated self-perform services. Buffalo Atlee provides a specific generation-construction example.
scopes.boundary: Technology, engineering, fuel, ownership, operation and power supply remain project-specific; construction capability is not an energy-supply commitment.

valueMechanisms.schedule: Sequence generation installation with electrical receiving works and the agreed energization plan
valueMechanisms.cost: Define generation tie-ins and enabling works before releasing their packages
valueMechanisms.risk: Make generation, utility and owner dependencies visible before interfaces are committed
valueMechanisms.quality: Align installation checks with equipment requirements and electrical receiving criteria
valueMechanisms.safety: Plan lifting, access and electrical work zones around adjacent campus activities
valueMechanisms.coordination: Connect generation, civil and electrical teams at the campus connection points

scopes.label: HV/MV powerlines
scopes.headline: Carry the power route through the delivery plan
scopes.documentedCapability: Bird explicitly lists high- and medium-voltage powerlines within integrated self-perform services.
scopes.boundary: Route rights, utility capacity, connection agreements, outages and energization approval are external or project-specific. The line is shown as an illustrative 230 kV route on lattice towers.

valueMechanisms.schedule: Align line-route workfaces with substation and civil readiness
valueMechanisms.cost: Clarify route, crossing and termination scope before package release
valueMechanisms.risk: Track utility and crossing dependencies alongside Bird-delivered work
valueMechanisms.quality: Retain line-installation checks and termination acceptance at each receiving interface
valueMechanisms.safety: Coordinate access and electrical exclusion zones along the power corridor
valueMechanisms.coordination: Join powerline, substation and site-civil planning at each route interface

scopes.label: Substations
scopes.headline: Make the electrical receiving point a shared plan
scopes.documentedCapability: Bird lists substations within integrated self-perform services for mission-critical and data-centre delivery.
scopes.boundary: Equipment supply, utility protection requirements, grid allocation and energization authority require agreement; delivery does not grant approval rights.

valueMechanisms.schedule: Connect substation civil readiness, equipment placement and electrical installation dates
valueMechanisms.cost: Define equipment foundations, cable entries and installation boundaries together
valueMechanisms.risk: Expose protection, utility and equipment dependencies before testing is planned
valueMechanisms.quality: Carry inspection requirements from equipment receiving to installation and package tests
valueMechanisms.safety: Coordinate heavy lifts, access routes and electrical work zones at the receiving point
valueMechanisms.coordination: Connect civil, powerline, electrical and test-team information at one physical interface

scopes.label: Telecommunications
scopes.headline: Keep communications routes connected to the build
scopes.documentedCapability: Bird lists telecommunications within its integrated self-perform services.
scopes.boundary: Confirm fibre, network equipment, controls, security and operator IT boundaries; telecom capability does not establish ownership of every IT system. Fibre is shown along the transmission towers and underground into the meet-me room.

valueMechanisms.schedule: Align telecom route access with containment, enclosure and white-space readiness
valueMechanisms.cost: Clarify pathway and termination allowances before adjacent installations close access
valueMechanisms.risk: Make carrier, operator and equipment interfaces explicit before service connections
valueMechanisms.quality: Retain pathway, labelling and agreed test records for the telecom scope
valueMechanisms.safety: Plan telecom access around active electrical and overhead installation work
valueMechanisms.coordination: Coordinate telecom routes with electrical, mechanical and operator connection points

scopes.label: Thermal energy transfer
scopes.headline: Connect thermal interfaces to the campus systems
scopes.documentedCapability: Bird explicitly lists thermal-energy transfer within integrated self-perform services.
scopes.boundary: Thermal network ownership, technology selection, operating conditions and energy outcomes remain project-specific; no efficiency result is implied.

valueMechanisms.schedule: Align thermal route, plant connection and receiving-system readiness
valueMechanisms.cost: Define thermal connection points and installation responsibilities before release
valueMechanisms.risk: Expose external network and plant dependencies alongside the thermal package
valueMechanisms.quality: Retain inspection and test requirements across buried, plant and building connections
valueMechanisms.safety: Coordinate thermal installation access with civil and mechanical workfaces
valueMechanisms.coordination: Connect site-civil, mechanical and energy-provider requirements at thermal interfaces

scopes.label: Earthworks
scopes.headline: Prepare the workfaces that follow
scopes.documentedCapability: Bird lists earthworks for data centres and earthmoving in its self-perform capability.
scopes.boundary: Ground conditions, environmental constraints, disposal arrangements and the project-specific excavation scope require confirmation.

valueMechanisms.schedule: Sequence excavation and grading around utility and foundation workface releases
valueMechanisms.cost: Bring delivery input to quantities, access and material-handling assumptions
valueMechanisms.risk: Make ground and buried-service constraints visible before downstream crews mobilize
valueMechanisms.quality: Retain agreed formation checks before the next trade receives the workface
valueMechanisms.safety: Coordinate excavation access, plant movement and separation from adjacent activities
valueMechanisms.coordination: Connect earthworks handovers to utility installation and concrete preparation

scopes.label: Underground utilities
scopes.headline: Connect below-ground work to electrical readiness
scopes.documentedCapability: Bird explicitly lists buried utilities within integrated self-perform services.
scopes.boundary: Confirm the utility types, routes and handover split. Inspections and receiving-trade acceptance remain required.

valueMechanisms.schedule: Align trench release, duct installation and electrical receiving workfaces
valueMechanisms.cost: Resolve route, excavation and reinstatement boundaries before release
valueMechanisms.risk: Identify buried crossings and receiving interfaces before access is closed
valueMechanisms.quality: Retain utility inspection and as-built checks before backfill and handover
valueMechanisms.safety: Coordinate trench access and adjacent plant movements with the installation sequence
valueMechanisms.coordination: Connect civil and electrical planning at the actual duct and cable-entry interfaces

scopes.label: Concrete formwork
scopes.headline: Carry concrete interfaces into systems planning
scopes.documentedCapability: Bird lists concrete formwork for mission-critical delivery and concrete in its broader self-perform offer.
scopes.boundary: Confirm concrete package allocation. These sources do not establish every foundation, geotechnical, structural steel or enclosure scope.

valueMechanisms.schedule: Align concrete releases with service entries and equipment-support readiness
valueMechanisms.cost: Resolve formwork, penetration and embedded-item responsibilities before pours
valueMechanisms.risk: Expose service and equipment-interface requirements before concrete work is fixed
valueMechanisms.quality: Retain pre-pour checks and agreed acceptance before following trades receive the area
valueMechanisms.safety: Plan pours, access and temporary workfaces around adjacent installation activities
valueMechanisms.coordination: Bring civil, electrical and mechanical requirements together at concrete interfaces

scopes.label: Electrical
scopes.headline: Connect the electrical installation to its workfaces
scopes.documentedCapability: Bird explicitly lists electrical within integrated self-perform services; its broader offer includes electrical and instrumentation.
scopes.boundary: Confirm package boundaries, equipment supply, protection/controls, utility roles and test responsibilities. Full IST and owner acceptance are separate.

valueMechanisms.schedule: Align electrical installation with released duct routes, rooms and equipment access
valueMechanisms.cost: Bring field input to containment, termination and installation scope before release
valueMechanisms.risk: Keep civil, OEM and commissioning dependencies visible in the electrical plan
valueMechanisms.quality: Carry workmanship checks and traceable records into package testing
valueMechanisms.safety: Coordinate isolation planning and electrical work zones with adjacent trades
valueMechanisms.coordination: Connect electrical routes and receiving points with civil and mechanical teams

scopes.label: Mechanical
scopes.headline: Connect mechanical work from fabrication to site
scopes.documentedCapability: Bird lists mechanical as integrated self-perform capability and process mechanical in its broader offer.
scopes.boundary: Confirm equipment supply, process requirements, fabrication capacity, installation split and manufacturer responsibilities.

valueMechanisms.schedule: Align mechanical fabrication, delivery access and field installation workfaces
valueMechanisms.cost: Resolve package connections and field-fit requirements before fabrication release
valueMechanisms.risk: Identify equipment and adjoining-system dependencies before installation
valueMechanisms.quality: Carry fabrication and installation checks through to agreed mechanical test records
valueMechanisms.safety: Coordinate lifts and mechanical installation access with electrical and civil work
valueMechanisms.coordination: Connect mechanical, electrical and fabrication information at shared plant interfaces

scopes.label: HVAC and refrigeration
scopes.headline: Make cooling installation part of the shared sequence
scopes.documentedCapability: Bird explicitly lists HVAC and refrigeration within integrated self-perform services.
scopes.boundary: Cooling design duty, redundancy, selected technology, controls, OEM obligations and operating performance require project confirmation. Roof-mounted cooling units are shown at campus density.

valueMechanisms.schedule: Align cooling installation with enclosure, power and plant-access readiness
valueMechanisms.cost: Clarify cooling equipment connections and access provisions before release
valueMechanisms.risk: Expose cooling, electrical and controls dependencies before functional-test planning
valueMechanisms.quality: Retain agreed installation checks and evidence at cooling-system interfaces
valueMechanisms.safety: Coordinate cooling-equipment lifts and access with adjacent overhead work
valueMechanisms.coordination: Connect cooling layouts with electrical routes, mechanical services and controls

scopes.label: White-space deployment
scopes.headline: Define the delivery boundary inside the hall
scopes.documentedCapability: Bird lists white-space deployment as part of its broader mission-critical delivery offer.
scopes.boundary: The full self-perform split is not established. Confirm racks, containment, controls, fire/security, network and operator IT responsibilities. The orange floor line marks where grey space ends and white space begins. Integrated white-space fit-out depends on the agreed scope.

valueMechanisms.schedule: Align white-space access with room readiness and released power and cooling interfaces
valueMechanisms.cost: Define installation and owner-supplied equipment boundaries before fit-out release
valueMechanisms.risk: Make operator, vendor and trade responsibilities visible at each hall interface
valueMechanisms.quality: Agree receiving checks and records for the white-space package
valueMechanisms.safety: Coordinate fit-out access around active plant and overhead installation activities
valueMechanisms.coordination: Connect hall layouts with electrical, cooling, telecom and operator requirements

scopes.label: Commissioning support
scopes.headline: Prepare the evidence that readiness needs
scopes.documentedCapability: Bird explicitly lists commissioning support in its mission-critical and data-centre offer.
scopes.boundary: Support does not establish full data-centre IST ownership, independent commissioning authority, certification or owner acceptance.

valueMechanisms.schedule: Connect construction closeout and package-test evidence with the agreed commissioning sequence
valueMechanisms.cost: Define support tasks, attendance and records before commissioning activities are released
valueMechanisms.risk: Track missing evidence and unresolved interfaces before readiness reviews
valueMechanisms.quality: Link installation records and outstanding items to agreed acceptance criteria
valueMechanisms.safety: Coordinate test access and isolation interfaces with the responsible parties
valueMechanisms.coordination: Bring construction, test-team and operator information together at readiness gates

scopes.label: High-voltage testing
scopes.headline: Prove the agreed electrical package
scopes.documentedCapability: Bird’s 2025 MD&A identifies high-voltage testing and commissioning as industrial self-perform services.
scopes.boundary: This is general industrial evidence. Confirm the data-centre electrical test package; it does not establish full IST, independent certification, utility energization or owner acceptance.

valueMechanisms.schedule: Align the agreed HV test sequence with installation completion and access readiness
valueMechanisms.cost: Define test boundaries, attendance and records before electrical package release
valueMechanisms.risk: Separate package-test prerequisites from utility and owner approval gates
valueMechanisms.quality: Retain test evidence and defect resolution against agreed electrical criteria
valueMechanisms.safety: Coordinate test zones and isolation responsibilities before HV test activities
valueMechanisms.coordination: Connect electrical installation records with the test team and receiving parties

scopes.label: Expansion works
scopes.headline: Connect the next phase to the existing campus
scopes.documentedCapability: Bird lists facility expansions within its mission-critical scope and describes sensitive upgrades within its industrial maintenance work.
scopes.boundary: Confirm direct-delivery packages, live-site constraints and outage responsibilities. Work in existing or occupied environments is not described on the current public pages and needs confirmation. No capacity, uptime or expansion-date commitment is established.

valueMechanisms.schedule: Plan new workfaces around retained access and agreed live-site connection windows
valueMechanisms.cost: Use existing-interface information to define the next-phase scope before release
valueMechanisms.risk: Expose existing-asset and operator constraints before expansion tie-ins
valueMechanisms.quality: Keep new-work inspections and existing-system receiving checks distinct
valueMechanisms.safety: Separate expansion work areas from operating-site access and activities
valueMechanisms.coordination: Connect original delivery knowledge with the operator and next-phase teams

scopes.label: Maintenance capability
scopes.headline: Keep maintenance scope connected to asset knowledge
scopes.documentedCapability: Bird describes industrial civil, mechanical, electrical and instrumentation maintenance, troubleshooting and sensitive upgrades.
scopes.boundary: Confirm data-centre applicability and scope. No facilities-operation role, IT service, staffing level, operating SLA or uptime guarantee is established.

valueMechanisms.schedule: Plan agreed maintenance activities around operator access and service windows
valueMechanisms.cost: Define asset condition, access and maintenance boundaries before the work is released
valueMechanisms.risk: Identify existing-system and operator dependencies before intrusive work
valueMechanisms.quality: Link maintenance records and agreed checks to the affected asset
valueMechanisms.safety: Coordinate access and isolation responsibilities with the operating-site team
valueMechanisms.coordination: Carry relevant installation and asset information into the agreed maintenance scope

scopes.label: Planning and design coordination
scopes.headline: Bring delivery knowledge into early decisions
scopes.documentedCapability: Bird describes preconstruction, buildability, BIM/VDC, procurement/logistics and specialist design-team coordination.
scopes.boundary: Design partners and engineers retain their agreed roles. Architect/engineer-of-record status, feasibility conclusions and procurement commitments are project-specific.

valueMechanisms.schedule: Bring trade sequencing and procurement dependencies into early campus planning
valueMechanisms.cost: Use delivery-team input to define quantities, scope boundaries and budget assumptions
valueMechanisms.risk: Expose buildability, approval and interface uncertainties before package release
valueMechanisms.quality: Connect coordinated design information to work-package inspection requirements
valueMechanisms.safety: Review access, lifting areas and adjacent workfaces before site mobilization
valueMechanisms.coordination: Connect design partners, trade teams and procurement around shared interfaces

scopes.label: Permit authority
scopes.headline: Keep approvals visible as external gates
scopes.documentedCapability: Bird/Stack collateral describes management of permitting in a modular offer. It does not establish a data-centre approval mandate; approval decisions remain external.
scopes.boundary: Identify the actual authorities, required studies and applicant responsibilities. Managing a submission is not issuing or guaranteeing an approval.

valueMechanisms.schedule: Show submission and approval dependencies before civil and utility release dates
valueMechanisms.cost: Identify approval conditions that could change quantities or installation scope
valueMechanisms.risk: Keep unresolved approval requirements visible in the project dependency plan
valueMechanisms.quality: Connect approved requirements to the documents used for construction checks
valueMechanisms.safety: Carry relevant permit conditions into workface and access planning
valueMechanisms.coordination: Clarify who prepares, submits, reviews and approves each required application

scopes.label: Structure and enclosure
scopes.headline: Keep the base build connected to installation access
scopes.documentedCapability: Bird’s mission-critical offer includes civil and structural construction; concrete formwork is explicitly self-perform.
scopes.boundary: Confirm steel, envelope and base-build package allocation. General structural delivery does not prove whole-shell self-performance.

valueMechanisms.schedule: Align enclosure readiness and equipment access with plant installation
valueMechanisms.cost: Define openings, supports and temporary-access responsibilities before release
valueMechanisms.risk: Expose structural and weather-tightness dependencies in the systems-installation plan
valueMechanisms.quality: Retain structural and enclosure checks before rooms are handed to installation teams
valueMechanisms.safety: Coordinate structural work, lifting routes and systems access across shared areas
valueMechanisms.coordination: Connect base-build information with concrete, mechanical and electrical interfaces

scopes.label: Owner acceptance
scopes.headline: Keep the final acceptance decision explicit
scopes.documentedCapability: Bird documents commissioning support and industrial HV testing; the reviewed evidence does not assign owner acceptance to Bird.
scopes.boundary: Agree the owner/operator’s criteria and decision rights. Package tests, full IST, independent commissioning review and final acceptance are distinct.

valueMechanisms.schedule: Make acceptance prerequisites visible before the planned handover gate
valueMechanisms.cost: Define required evidence and unresolved-scope treatment before closeout
valueMechanisms.risk: Keep open items and decision ownership visible until the owner’s acceptance process is complete
valueMechanisms.quality: Map test and inspection records to the owner’s agreed acceptance criteria
valueMechanisms.safety: Coordinate the transition from construction work zones to operator-controlled access
valueMechanisms.coordination: Connect contractor records, commissioning review and the owner’s acceptance decision

scopes.label: Energy sources
scopes.headline: Connect the energy mix to the campus
scopes.documentedCapability: Bird lists power generation within its integrated self-perform services and describes energy construction capability including hydro and pumped storage, wind, solar, and nuclear and SMRs.
scopes.boundary: The energy mix is illustrative. The gas-fired plant is shown at the mission critical team's request; confirm its public evidence before client use. Technology, fuel, ownership and offtake remain project-specific.

valueMechanisms.schedule: Sequence generation, collector and transmission works with the campus energization plan
valueMechanisms.cost: Define the interfaces between generation, transmission and campus receiving works before packages are released
valueMechanisms.risk: Make generation, utility and owner dependencies visible early
valueMechanisms.quality: Align construction checks with each generation technology's requirements
valueMechanisms.safety: Plan heavy lifts, access and energized work zones across separate generation sites
valueMechanisms.coordination: Connect generation, transmission and campus teams around one energy plan

scopes.label: HV power skids
scopes.headline: Prefabricated power, set where it is needed
scopes.documentedCapability: Bird self-performs fabrication, including specialty modular work, and fabricates electrical houses and specialty modular skid units.
scopes.boundary: Generic skids are shown. Skid design ownership is being confirmed, so no proprietary skid or piping detail is depicted. Ratings, design and supply remain project-specific.

valueMechanisms.schedule: Build skids off site in parallel with civil and building works
valueMechanisms.cost: Fix skid scope and interfaces early with the trades that receive them
valueMechanisms.risk: Move assembly and factory checks away from the congested site
valueMechanisms.quality: Assemble and inspect in a controlled shop before shipping
valueMechanisms.safety: Reduce work at height and in congested electrical rooms on site
valueMechanisms.coordination: Connect fabrication, logistics and installation crews through one plan

scopes.label: Skidded UPS room
scopes.headline: Open a prefabricated room down to its components
scopes.documentedCapability: Bird self-performs fabrication and lists electrical houses among its fabrication capabilities. This module shows how a prefabricated UPS room can carry its equipment, logistics and commissioning records together.
scopes.boundary: Component counts, logistics and commissioning states are illustrative sample data, not a project record or a protected design. Equipment supply and integration remain project-specific.

valueMechanisms.schedule: Track fabrication, delivery and set dates for each module
valueMechanisms.cost: Know the equipment quantities in each module before release
valueMechanisms.risk: See open factory and site test items before energization
valueMechanisms.quality: Carry factory test records with the module to site
valueMechanisms.safety: Plan lifts and energization around each module's status
valueMechanisms.coordination: Share one record across fabrication, logistics and commissioning

scopes.label: OFCI management
scopes.headline: Receive, install and track owner-furnished equipment
scopes.documentedCapability: The mission critical team identified management of owner-furnished, contractor-installed (OFCI) equipment as part of Bird's delivery story. No public Bird page describes it yet.
scopes.boundary: Internal input. Add the evidence and confirm the wording before client use. Responsibilities follow the agreed contract.

valueMechanisms.schedule: Align owner equipment deliveries with installation workfaces
valueMechanisms.cost: Separate owner-furnished and contractor-supplied scope early
valueMechanisms.risk: Make receiving, storage and warranty responsibilities explicit
valueMechanisms.quality: Inspect owner equipment on receipt and record its condition
valueMechanisms.safety: Plan lifts and handling for heavy owner equipment
valueMechanisms.coordination: Connect owner procurement with site installation and commissioning

sources.title: Mission Critical & Data Centres
sources.evidenceSummary: Lists integrated self-perform services (power generation, high and medium voltage powerlines, telecommunication, substations, thermal energy transfer systems, earth works, underground utilities, concrete formwork, electrical, mechanical, HVAC and refrigeration) and a broader mission-critical scope that includes civil and structural construction, utility and substation upgrades, white-space deployment, facility expansions and commissioning support. Names a White Space Solutions lead.
sources.boundary: Does not establish project-specific labour allocation, local availability, full IST, independent commissioning authority or an outcome guarantee.

sources.title: Pre-Construction / Early Contractor Involvement
sources.evidenceSummary: Describes preconstruction advice, procurement and logistics, integrated schedules, estimating and risk mitigation.
sources.boundary: Does not establish land acquisition, permit issuance, utility capacity or guaranteed procurement dates.

sources.title: Industrial Maintenance
sources.evidenceSummary: Describes industrial civil, mechanical, electrical and instrumentation maintenance, troubleshooting, ongoing work and sensitive upgrades.
sources.boundary: Data-centre maintenance scope, staffing, operating SLA, IT services and uptime obligations require confirmation.

sources.title: BIM/VDC
sources.evidenceSummary: Describes BIM/VDC coordination, visualization, schedule planning and coordinated mechanical and electrical information.
sources.boundary: Does not establish architect or engineer-of-record responsibility or live integration with this concept.

sources.title: Self-Perform
sources.evidenceSummary: Lists directly delivered trades (earth works, concrete, process mechanical, electrical and instrumentation) and fabrication (mass modular, specialty modular, pipe, metal); connects self-performance with control over schedule, costs and quality.
sources.boundary: Qualitative Bird positioning does not establish quantified project improvement or comparative proof.

sources.title: Future Energy Hub
sources.evidenceSummary: Connects self-perform expertise with early planning, construction-led sequencing and critical-path trade delivery alongside technology and engineering partners.
sources.boundary: Does not establish ownership of every technology, power supply, grid allocation, energy prices or carbon outcomes.

sources.title: Construction Management
sources.evidenceSummary: Describes cost-benefit analysis, lifecycle costing, value engineering, tendering and project controls within construction management.
sources.boundary: Supports commercial planning, not a project estimate or promised saving.

sources.title: Fabrication
sources.evidenceSummary: Describes specialty skids, electrical houses, water modules and process piping, with team communication from design through commissioning.
sources.boundary: Does not promise a factory slot, standard data-centre module, lead-time saving or off-site proportion.

sources.title: 2025 MD&A, printed p. 6
sources.evidenceSummary: The industrial section identifies high-voltage testing and commissioning among self-perform services; buildings coverage includes data-centre lifecycle delivery.
sources.boundary: Industrial electrical testing does not establish full data-centre IST, independent commissioning authority, certification or owner acceptance.

sources.title: Quality
sources.evidenceSummary: Describes job-specific quality-control planning, quality management and assurance procedures.
sources.boundary: Do not assume every division or project holds the same certification, or guarantee defect-free work or first-pass acceptance.

sources.title: Safety
sources.evidenceSummary: Describes pre-project safety planning, onboarding, hazard management, monitoring and workforce participation.
sources.boundary: Does not establish that self-performance causes fewer injuries or comparative safety superiority.

sources.title: Civil Infrastructure
sources.evidenceSummary: Describes underground services, earthworks, concrete, hydro work, drilling, blasting and site servicing.
sources.boundary: Does not establish a specific crew allocation or permit mandate.

sources.title: Mission-critical project-experience landing page
sources.evidenceSummary: This address redirected to the Mission Critical & Data Centres page (B1) on 6 October 2026. The earlier summary of this landing page (greenfield work, occupied environments, fit-outs, prefabrication, early design collaboration, as-built scanning) could not be found on the page it now serves.
sources.boundary: Cite B1 instead. Establishes nothing separate from B1.

sources.title: Data Centres brochure, older undated collateral
sources.evidenceSummary: Older data-centre collateral describes Canem and complementary electrical, mechanical, communications, technology, commissioning, white-space and maintenance services.
sources.boundary: Older undated collateral has lower currency confidence. Prefer B1 for current headline scope; subsidiary experience does not establish every Bird team’s capability.
sources.currency: Historical or older collateral. The link returned HTTP 404 on 5 October 2026: confirm or replace the document before client use.

sources.title: Buffalo Atlee Wind
sources.evidenceSummary: A specific wind project records Bird as prime EPC contractor, self-performing a majority of the work, with testing, commissioning and energization in its delivery scope.
sources.boundary: Development, ownership and operation are attributed to Capstone. This does not establish Bird energy-supply ownership or data-centre power availability.

sources.title: Bell / Sherwood announcement, 14 May 2026
sources.evidenceSummary: The May 2026 announcement identifies Bird as a construction partner for the planned Sherwood AI facility and names outside design and site-services roles.
sources.boundary: Forward-looking project selection is not completion. Named partners demonstrate that integrated delivery is not wholly self-performed.

sources.title: Bird and Stack: Building Tomorrow, November 2024, printed p. 4
sources.evidenceSummary: Bird and Stack modular collateral describes management of feasibility, site selection, permitting, design, engineering and estimating.
sources.boundary: This is an adjacent-sector offer. Data-centre applicability is unconfirmed; management does not confer approval authority or establish land acquisition.

sources.title: The Centre for Building Performance
sources.evidenceSummary: Describes building-performance analytics for energy use, equipment anomalies and emissions-related monitoring.
sources.boundary: Does not establish live integration with this concept, a data-centre operating SLA, a DCIM replacement or efficiency outcomes.

sources.title: Delivery Models
sources.evidenceSummary: Describes delivery models and specialist design-team assembly, including design-build and EPC.
sources.boundary: Integrated delivery models are not themselves proof of whole-scope self-performance.

sources.title: 2023 Annual Report, printed p. 39
sources.evidenceSummary: The 2023 annual report describes Sigma Power MV/HV maintenance, commissioning, protection/control and SCADA, plus fabrication-related electrical integration.
sources.boundary: Historical and business-specific evidence; current deployment requires confirmation. Prefer B9 for newer self-perform electrical testing evidence.

callToAction.label: Map Bird's scope to your project
callToAction.description: Confirm delivery boundaries, local capability, external responsibilities and the evidence needed for your project.

buildSequence.note: One guided sequence through the energy chain and the construction layers. Completed scopes turn transparent; the current scope is in colour.

energy.text: An illustrative energy mix: nuclear and SMR, gas-fired, hydro, wind and solar generation feeding the campus.

transmission.text: An illustrative 230 kV line on lattice towers carries power to the campus fence.

substation.text: Transformers, breakers and protection step the voltage down for campus distribution.

earthworks.text: Site levels, access and excavation set up every workface that follows.

utilities.text: Duct banks carry power and fibre below grade, coordinated while they can still be seen.

concrete.text: Slabs, pads and trench walls fix where every package sits.

steel.text: The frame and envelope close in the protected environment.

electrical.text: Prefabricated HV skids, skidded UPS rooms and MV switchgear feed busway with a drop into every rack.

mechanical.text: Plant, thermal mains and roof-mounted cooling units reject the heat.

whitespace.text: Fibre runs along the towers and underground into the meet-me room. The orange line marks where grey space ends and white space begins.

commissioning.text: Package testing, commissioning support and owner acceptance prove the facility is ready.

commissioning.label: Level 5 · Integrated systems test, scope to confirm

steps.text: Power generation is only the start. One integrated Bird team walks the client along the whole path, from energy source to white space.

photo.shot: Bird crew on an energy project such as wind or hydro construction, Bird branding and full PPE visible
photo.alt: Bird crew in full PPE on an energy project site

steps.text: Every source feeds one high-voltage substation. Substations are part of the work Bird delivers.

photo.shot: Bird electrical crew at a high-voltage substation, Bird branding and full PPE visible
photo.alt: Bird electrical crew in full PPE at a high-voltage substation

steps.text: High-voltage lines carry the power on lattice towers toward the campus. Bird self-performs high and medium voltage powerlines.

photo.shot: Bird crew building a powerline, for example on a lattice tower or stringing conductor, full PPE
photo.alt: Bird crew in full PPE working on a transmission line

steps.text: The line comes down into the campus substation. Generation stays in view, because the whole ecosystem is connected.

photo.shot: Bird crew setting or connecting a transformer at a substation, Bird branding and full PPE visible
photo.alt: Bird crew in full PPE working at a substation transformer

steps.text: The site starts empty. Bird’s civil teams excavate it and cut the trenches that carry every utility.

photo.shot: Bird crew and excavators opening a site, for example at Sherwood, Bird branding and full PPE visible
photo.alt: Bird civil crew and excavators opening a site

steps.text: Power, chilled water, fibre and storm lines share the trench network, and coordinating them is a huge effort. Bird self-performs underground utilities.

photo.shot: Bird crew laying duct bank conduit in an open trench, for example at Sherwood, full PPE
photo.alt: Bird crew in full PPE installing duct bank conduit in a trench

steps.text: Slabs and equipment pads are poured over the utilities, and the underground work disappears from view. Bird forms and pours the concrete.

photo.shot: Bird crew placing concrete with an industrial pumping truck, for example at Sherwood or Fort McMurray
photo.alt: Bird crew placing concrete with a pumping truck

steps.text: The steel frame rises and the building starts to close in, delivered with specialist partners.

photo.shot: Bird industrial crew erecting structural steel, Bird branding and full PPE visible
photo.alt: Bird industrial crew in full PPE erecting structural steel

steps.text: Electrical powers the grey space first, up to the white space. Bird self-performs the electrical work.

photo.shot: Bird electricians terminating cable at a switchgear lineup, Bird branding and full PPE visible
photo.alt: Bird electricians in full PPE terminating cable at switchgear

steps.text: Chilled water runs underground from the chiller yard into the building, up to the white space. Bird self-performs mechanical, HVAC and refrigeration.

photo.shot: Bird pipefitters installing chilled water piping or setting a chiller, full PPE
photo.alt: Bird pipefitters in full PPE installing chilled water piping

steps.text: Equipment can be built off site as modules, then rolled in as it arrives. Bird fabricates specialty skids and electrical houses.

photo.shot: Bird shop crew assembling a skid or electrical house off site, full PPE
photo.alt: Bird shop crew assembling a skid in a fabrication shop

steps.text: Telecom arrives on its own pole line and runs into the meet-me room, stopping at the white space. Bird self-performs telecommunications.

photo.shot: Bird crew pulling fibre or setting a telecom pole line, full PPE
photo.alt: Bird crew in full PPE installing fibre or a telecom pole

steps.text: White space is its own scope with its own Bird team, built last. Electrical, mechanical and telecom come together here at once.

photo.shot: Bird crew installing racks, containment or busway in a data hall, full PPE
photo.alt: Bird crew in full PPE installing racks and containment in a data hall
